meta.title: Healthstack
meta.description: A specialized IDE for lifestyle optimization on Eclipse Theia: biomarker tracking, unit conversion, and a purpose-built DSL for intervention protocols. Currently a private dev build.
meta.imageAlt: Biomarker dashboard in the Healthstack dev build

head.tryLanguage: Try the language in your browser

intro: Protocols as code, biology as data, AI as your cortex. A protocol is a `.bio` file, so it validates as you type and versions in git like any other source. Lab values are tracked against their reference ranges, a timeline lines up what was planned with what happened, and a team of agents reads all of it. Healthstack is local-first.

preview.label: Preview
preview.body: Everything on this page is the dev build: it runs, the DSL compiles, the diagnostics fire. Expect rough edges, no data guarantees, and no product promises. The screenshots are real, taken from the app as it works today. A public preview is not hosted yet; the language is, in the playground below.

language.heading: The language
language.body: Protocols are data, not prose, and the language's type system is written in the language itself: `substance`, `intervention`, `stack`, and `protocol` are user-extendable `type` declarations in `.bio`, not hardcoded in the grammar. The editor below runs the real language server in this tab. Your data never leaves your machine. It opens with a sample that defines its own types, then extends them; the other samples cover a curated supplement library and the live interaction checker.
language.caption: Live - .bio language server, running in this tab
language.fallbackLabel: Playground not bundled with this build
language.fallbackBody: The .bio language server is not included here. Run the full build chain to embed the live editor on this page.

sections.heading: Timeline
sections.body: Every protocol, dose, and threshold on *one axis*: planned against actual, with threshold events armed and crossed, dose dots per phase, and the whole history exportable to your calendar.
sections.imageAlt: Unified timeline from July to December 2026: the Metabolic Reset phases Prep, Insulin Sensitivity, Lipid Optimization and Maintenance as dashed planned bars with dose dots above solid actual bars, a red NOW marker, and daily HRV, resting heart rate, sleep and step readings below with amber threshold-armed points.
sections.caption: Dev build - timeline

sections.heading: Protocol builder
sections.body: Protocols are composed as a graph, not a spreadsheet. Substances are nodes, synergies and conflicts are edges, and tracks reach from protocol to biomarker. The graph lays itself out again as you edit, and because a protocol is text, it versions in git.
sections.imageAlt: Protocol Builder graph of the Metabolic Reset protocol: the protocol node fans out to four phases, ten interventions and four substances, dotted blue track edges run to ten biomarkers, and a red dashed conflict edge links Berberine and Metformin.
sections.caption: Dev build - protocol builder

sections.heading: Biomarker tracker
sections.body: Each lab value sits against its reference range with a status: optimal, good, or out. Sparklines show the trend, and units convert as you paste, mg/dL to mmol/L and back.
sections.imageAlt: Biomarker Tracker overview table: LDL cholesterol flagged Out of Range at 104 mg/dL, followed by markers rated Good or Optimal, each with its latest value and unit, a bar showing its position in the range, a sparkline and a percentage trend.
sections.caption: Dev build - biomarker tracker

sections.heading: Trends
sections.body: The curve, not just the number: several markers compared on one chart, range bands drawn over time, event markers where protocols started or ended, values normalized across different labs, and a hand-off to the agents for analysis.
sections.imageAlt: Two stacked trend charts on a shared April 2025 to October 2026 timeline: ApoB falling to 84 mg/dL and LDL cholesterol to 104 mg/dL toward shaded reference and optimal bands, both marked improving.
sections.caption: Dev build - trends

agents.heading: AI agents
agents.body: Cortex orchestrates *your Healthstack*: it takes each request and hands sub-questions to three specialists. The agents work on your biomarker database and your `.bio` files, and tool calls that change data ask for approval first. Bring your own key for the model provider you use.

list.name: @Cortex
list.description: The default agent. Routes each request, records data, drafts protocols, and delegates to the specialists.

list.name: @Evidence
list.description: Clinical reference grounded in the literature, which it searches through [med-research-mcp](route:project_med_research). Also interprets biomarkers and checks interactions.

list.name: @BiomarkerAnalyst
list.description: Reads the biomarker database and summarizes trends and out-of-range markers.

list.name: @ProtocolPlanner
list.description: Composes valid `.bio` protocol files for you to review and approve.

agents.imageAlt: Ask Cortex chat panel beside the Protocol Builder graph, with suggested prompts addressed to @BiomarkerAnalyst, @Evidence and @ProtocolPlanner and a note that agent tool calls ask for confirmation first.
